parameters.name: k0
parameters.note: Coefficient k of the family; the surface is continuous in it, so dragging it walks the family through its transitions

parameters.name: k1
parameters.note: Coefficient k' of the family; the surface is continuous in it, so dragging it walks the family through its transitions

parameters.name: k2
parameters.note: Coefficient k'' of the family; the surface is continuous in it, so dragging it walks the family through its transitions

parameters.name: k3
parameters.note: Coefficient k''' of the family; the surface is continuous in it, so dragging it walks the family through its transitions

parameters.name: size
parameters.note: The length a the coefficients are measured against. It rescales the surface inside the clip ball rather than the finished object, so it changes how much is shown

provenance.definition: Closed form reproduced numerically against the shipped implementation (math_art/surfaces/algebraic.py) over 240 sample points: matches oracle x 1 over 240 points (worst 3.55e-14).
sources: A. Cayley, "A Memoir on Cubic Surfaces", Phil. Trans. 159, 1869.
A. Clebsch, "Ueber die Flachen vierter Ordnung...", Journal fur die reine und angewandte Mathematik 69, 1868 -- the diagonal surface.
W. Barth, "Two projective surfaces with many nodes admitting the symmetries of the icosahedron", J. Algebraic Geometry 5, 1996.
H. Hauser, "Bildergalerie algebraischer Flaechen", Universitaet Wien -- the named gallery surfaces in the _HAUSER block below.

St. Endrass, "A Projective Surface of Degree Eight with 168 Nodes", J. Algebraic Geom. 6 (1997) 325-334 -- also the source of the five-parameter D8 x Z2 octic family; the 160- and 165-nodal parameter values are published on O. Labs's Algebraic Surface
E. Goursat, 'Etude des surfaces qui admettent tous les plans de symetrie d'un polyedre regulier', Ann. Sci. ENS 3e serie 4 (1887).
